h1: The 6 Best Blackmagic Design Video Switchers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Blackmagic ATEM video switchers, from the Mini Pro to the SDI Extreme ISO, compared on inputs, ISO recording and streaming.
summary: The ATEM Mini Pro is our top pick because it brings four HDMI inputs, direct live streaming and a lower price bucket into one compact box. The ATEM SDI Pro ISO is the choice for broadcast-style SDI cameras with ethernet streaming, the Mini Pro ISO adds ISO recording, and the SDI Extreme ISO is the eight-input flagship.
intro: The first decision with a Blackmagic switcher is not Mini versus Extreme, it is HDMI versus SDI. HDMI cables are cheap and cameras have the ports, but they are fragile and limited to short runs. SDI uses locking BNC connectors that survive being kicked and stretch much farther, which is why a venue with cameras across a room or a stage tends to choose the SDI line. Pick the connector your cameras use before you compare features.

We ranked six distinct ATEM models on inputs, ISO recording, streaming and control, using only what the listings state. Where a listing is also sold as a bundle with cables, we treated it as the same model rather than a separate product. Specifications are sparse on several listings, so we note when input counts or outputs are not given and recommend checking the manufacturer page for the full list.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM Mini Pro HDMI Live Stream Switcher
products.verdict: Four HDMI inputs at 10-bit 4:2:2 and direct internet live streaming for multicamera shows.
products.description:
The ATEM Mini Pro is a compact HDMI switcher with four HDMI type A inputs at 10-bit 4:2:2, built for multicamera live streaming straight to the internet. Ten-bit 4:2:2 keeps colour cleaner than 8-bit, which matters for skin tones and graphics.

It ranks first because it delivers the core switching job with a built-in streaming engine at a lower bucket, $200 to $500, than every other model here. The Mini Pro ISO adds recording of each camera, but costs considerably more.

Ideal for church streams, podcasts and small events with up to four HDMI cameras. The caveat is that it cannot record each camera separately, so editing after the show means working from the program feed only.
products.idealFor: Small streams with up to four HDMI cameras.
products.skipIf: You need to record each camera separately.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Pro ISO Live Stream Switcher (SWATEMMXEPBPRISO)
products.verdict: Four 3G-SDI inputs, ethernet streaming and built-in ISO recording for production work.
products.description:
The SDI Pro ISO takes four 3G-SDI inputs, streams directly over ethernet and includes ISO recording in its feature list. SDI connectors lock in place and travel over long cables, which suits stages and larger rooms.

It ranks second because it adds the SDI cabling and ISO capture that the HDMI Mini Pro lacks, while costing more in the $500 and up bucket. It sits above the basic SDI model because of the ISO function.

It is built for productions with cameras across a venue. The caveat is the cost and complexity, since buyers with HDMI cameras would need converters and may not use the extra features.
products.idealFor: Venues and stages with SDI cameras.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM Mini Pro ISO HDMI Switcher
products.verdict: The Mini Pro with an ISO feature for multicamera streaming and post-show editing.
products.description:
The Mini Pro ISO shares the Mini Pro's four 10-bit 4:2:2 HDMI inputs and multicamera internet streaming, adding the ISO capability named in its title. ISO recording captures each input separately, so you can re-cut the show later.

It ranks third because it costs more than the standard Mini Pro for that extra, and the SDI Pro ISO offers sturdier connectors for the same function. It beats the Extreme for buyers who only need four HDMI inputs.

Best for creators who edit after streaming. The caveat is that ISO files take storage, so plan the drive capacity.
cons: Costs more than the Mini Pro
Needs fast storage for ISO files
products.idealFor: Creators who re-edit their live shows.
products.skipIf: You never edit after the stream.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Live Production Switcher (SWATEMMXEP)
products.verdict: A four-input SDI production switcher with ethernet control and USB-C output.
products.description:
The ATEM SDI is the plain SDI model, with four SDI inputs, ethernet control and a USB-C 2.0 interface. Ethernet control means you can run the switcher from a laptop or panel across a room.

It ranks fourth because it lacks the ISO recording that its Pro ISO sibling provides and it does not state built-in streaming in its summary. It lands in the $200 to $500 bucket, which is the entry point for SDI.

Suits a venue that already owns SDI cameras and needs a switcher without the extras. The caveat is that adding streaming means a computer connected over USB.
products.idealFor: Venues with SDI cameras and a PC for streaming.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM Mini Extreme HDMI Switcher
products.verdict: The larger HDMI Mini, with an expanded input and output count for bigger shows.
products.description:
The Mini Extreme is the bigger HDMI switcher in the Mini family, and its listing highlights total video inputs, total outputs and HDMI video inputs. The summary gives labels rather than numbers, so confirm the exact counts on the product page.

It ranks fifth because it costs significantly more than the Mini Pro, in the $500 and up bucket, and the listing offers few specifics. It beats the smaller models for buyers who have outgrown four inputs.

A fit for a production with many cameras, graphics and a clean outputs plan. The caveat is that the price jump matters only if you actually use the additional connections.
pros: More inputs than the Mini Pro
products.idealFor: Productions that have outgrown four HDMI inputs.

products.name: Blackmagic Design ATEM SDI Extreme ISO Live Stream Switcher Bundle with 8' Cable
products.verdict: Eight 3G-SDI inputs at 10-bit HD, ISO recording and multicamera streaming.
products.description:
The SDI Extreme ISO is the flagship in this lineup, with eight 3G-SDI, 10-bit HD switchable inputs and the feature-rich streaming and ISO set. Eight inputs support a venue with many cameras plus replay or graphics sources.

It ranks last in a list led by value, because it costs the most and only suits productions with that many SDI sources. As a pure capability machine, though, it outclasses every other entry.

Best for a house of worship, school or event team running a full multi-camera show. The caveat is the investment: it needs cameras, cable and operators to justify the price.
products.skipIf: You run three or four cameras.

whatMatters.detail: HDMI is common on consumer cameras but fragile and short-range, while SDI locks in place and runs long distances. Choose by the cameras you own. Check the connector type on every camera, and budget for converters if you mix, since adapters add cost and potential failure points.

ISO recording saves each camera feed separately in addition to the program mix, so you can fix mistakes later. It needs storage and bandwidth. Look for ISO in the model name, and plan for fast external drives, since several 1080p streams write at once.

Some models stream directly to the internet over ethernet, so no computer is needed. Others output to USB for a PC to stream. Check the listing for direct streaming or ethernet, especially if you want a simple appliance that works without software at the venue.

Ten-bit 4:2:2 keeps more colour and tonal detail than 8-bit 4:2:0, which helps with skin tones and keying. It matters most when you grade or composite. Look for the bit depth in the specs, and remember your cameras must also output it to benefit.

Ethernet control lets software or a hardware panel run the switcher from across the room. Larger models add outputs and inputs. Check how the unit is controlled, and decide whether you need a physical panel or software on a laptop for the people operating the show.

faq.q: Do I need a computer with the ATEM Mini Pro?
faq.a: Not for streaming, since the Mini Pro streams straight to the internet over ethernet. You may still use a computer for control software or to adjust settings, but it is not required to go live.

faq.q: What mistake do people make buying a switcher?
faq.a: Buying by price without checking connectors. HDMI cameras cannot plug into the SDI Pro ISO without converters. Count your cameras and cable runs first, then pick between the HDMI Mini line and the SDI line.

faq.q: Is the Mini Pro ISO worth more than the Mini Pro?
faq.a: Only if you re-edit shows. The Pro ISO adds per-camera recording, but the base Mini Pro handles live streaming at a lower bucket. Skip the ISO premium for pure live events.

faq.q: How do I set up an ATEM for streaming?
faq.a: Connect cameras to the inputs, link ethernet to your network, then enter your streaming service details in the control software. Start with a test stream before going live to check upload speed and audio.

faq.q: How do I maintain a switcher?
faq.a: Keep firmware current through the manufacturer's software, avoid pulling HDMI cables by the cord and keep vents clear. Label your inputs and save a settings file so any volunteer can restore a show quickly.

faq.q: Can the Mini Extreme replace the Mini Pro?
faq.a: It can, with more inputs and outputs, but it sits in the $500 and up bucket. If four HDMI cameras cover your show, the Mini Pro is the better value.

finalTake: The ATEM Mini Pro is the best Blackmagic video switcher for most people because four HDMI inputs and direct streaming sit in a lower price bucket. Choose the SDI Pro ISO for SDI cameras and ISO recording, and the Mini Pro ISO for HDMI shows you edit. Match connectors to cameras first.
